title: GNSS interference monitor from u-blox telemetry and ADS-B NACp
summary: A stdlib heuristic scorer turns per-epoch receiver telemetry (C/N0 across SVs, AGC, CW jamming indicator, clock and position jumps, receiver spoofing/jamming flags) into jamming and spoofing scores, plus CUSUM consistency detectors for slow drag-off (position and Doppler velocity vs an IMU/odometry/static reference or a constant-velocity prior), clock-rate drift vs a learned oscillator rate, and lost fix as its own alert class. Alerts latch until explicit clear conditions hold, and every alert carries value, threshold, unit and evidence. A pyubx2 adapter feeds it from UBX NAV-PVT, NAV-SAT, NAV-STATUS, NAV-CLOCK, MON-RF and SEC-SIG. A second stdlib module applies the GPSJam percentage method to readsb aircraft.json NACp for area-level maps. Includes a note on what Galileo OSNMA changes.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06: 36 unit tests (29 scorer incl. 21 for the new consistency, lost-fix, latch and explanation logic with negative controls, 6 area map, 1 UBX replay) pass with pyubx2 1.4.1 on Python 3.12.14; 35 pass + 1 skipped stdlib-only on Python 3.14.7. Mutation check: disabling pos_drift, vel_mismatch, clock_drift, lost-fix, the latch, the noise-inflation cap or the CUSUM learning gate each fails 1-5 tests; letting references learn during a latched alarm fails none (not covered). Synthetic soak 20 h per mode: 0 alert epochs with the constant-velocity prior, 3 with a static reference. UBX replay of the synthetic capture: verdicts unchanged (109 clean / 30 jamming / 41 spoofing), alarm latched 60-98 s and 120-169 s with stated clear reasons. On real GNSS-SDR epochs from samples/gnss-signal-chain the drag-off was detected 6-9 s after the drag began (fix 11-21 m off) with no silent epoch afterwards, and the overpower/jam-then-spoof PVT outages raised lost-fix alarms. Not verified: live u-blox receiver, real recordings, real readsb feed, any OSNMA processing.
